title: Morgan Wallen, Garth Brooks, Taylor Swift & More Artists With Most Weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums Chart: Full List
summary: Male solo artists dominate, though three female solo artists and two groups have also achieved the feat.
body: Morgan Wallen ’s I’m the Problem leads Billboard ‘s Top Country Albums chart (dated Aug. 1) for the 46th nonconsecutive week. This ups Wallen’s career tally of weeks at No. 1 to 232, allowing him to extend his lead as the artist with the most weeks at No. 1 in the chart’s 62-year history. Wallen’s achievement is especially impressive because he has amassed this hefty total of weeks at No. 1 in a little less than six years. He first topped the chart on Aug. 15, 2020. Before returning to No. 1 last week, I’m the Problem spent 13 weeks at No. 2 behind Ella Langley ‘s Dandelion . That was the longest Wallen has been locked out of the top spot since he rose to superstar status in January 2021 with Dangerous: The Double Album . Top Country Albums originated as Hot Country Albums in the Jan. 11, 1964 issue of Billboard . Johnny Cash ’s Ring of Fire (The Best of Johnny Cash) headed the inaugural chart. The compilation was well-timed: “Ring of Fire” had headed Hot Country Songs for seven weeks the previous summer and had crossed over to reach the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100. title: Gracie Abrams Earns First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘Daughter From Hell’
summary: Plus, BTS’ ARIRANG surges back into the top 10 after new vinyl release.
body: Gracie Abrams scores her first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart as her third full-length studio effort, Daughter From Hell , debuts atop the Aug. 1-dated ranking. It starts with 124,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the week ending July 23, according to Luminate — the singer-songwriter’s best week ever by units. Abrams previously hit the top 10 with her last album, The Secret of Us , debuting and peaking at No. 2 in July 2024. title: Kacey Musgraves Cancels Three ‘Middle of Nowhere’ Tour Dates
summary: Musgraves has not publicly addressed the changes, and no explanation has been posted to her official social media accounts.
body: Kacey Musgraves has canceled three dates from her upcoming Middle of Nowhere tour, including what had been scheduled as the trek’s opening night. The canceled shows include the Aug. 20 performance at United Center in Chicago, the Aug. 29 show at TD Garden in Boston and the Sept. 2 concert at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. Fans were notified of the cancellations via emails from Ticketmaster, according to multiple reports and social media posts. “Please be advised that the Kacey Musgraves concert scheduled for Saturday, August 29, 2026 at TD Garden has been canceled,” one fan’s notice read, according to a screenshot shared on Reddit . “All tickets will be automatically refunded to fans at their original point of purchase. Please allow 7-10 business days for refunds to process.” No reason has been given for the cancellations. Musgraves has not publicly addressed the changes, and no explanation has been posted to her official social media accounts. The affected cities were all scheduled to host multiple Musgraves shows, and tickets for alternate dates in Chicago, Boston and New York remain available. The Middle of Nowhere tour is still scheduled to begin in Chicago on Aug. 21, acco…

title: Green Day’s Billie Joe Armstrong Unveils New Signature Guitar and Marshall Amp
summary: Both releases nod to the guitar tone Armstrong has used across decades of Green Day songs.
body: Billie Joe Armstrong has turned two pillars of his Green Day sound into new signature gear. The frontman has announced a limited-edition Radiant Red Epiphone Billie Joe Armstrong Les Paul Junior, along with his first artist signature amplifier with Marshall, the 1959BJA Artist Signature. Both releases nod to the stripped-down, high-impact guitar tone Armstrong has used across decades of Green Day songs, from the band’s 1994 breakthrough Dookie through its more recent stadium-scale era. The new Epiphone model features a bright red finish, similar to Armstrong’s Les Paul Junior, while maintaining a deliberately simple setup. The guitar features a single P-90 PRO pickup, master volume and tone controls, and a Lightning Bar wraparound bridge — a no-frills build in line with Armstrong’s long-running punk approach. The guitar also includes a reproduction of Armstrong’s signature on the back of the headstock and comes with a custom black hardshell case with a leopard-print interior. Armstrong’s new Marshall amp, meanwhile, marks the company’s first artist signature model in 14 years.
